name: Moray to the Maras salt pans
why: From the circular Inca terraces of Moray across the farm plateau to Maras, then down a gorge into thousands of white salt pools worked since Inca times.
book: Moray is on the Boleto Turístico del Cusco; the salt pans charge their own entry (about S/10, cash). Taxi or colectivo from Urubamba to Moray. From the salt pans a path goes down to the bridge over the Urubamba, where rides back are easy to find.
water: Shops in Maras village; carry 1.5 litres for the plateau.
dangers: Open plateau at 3,400 m: strong sun and wind, no shade.
Narrow walls between the salt pools: walk only where allowed, the edges crumble.
Steep, dusty path down the gorge below the salt pans.
turnaround: Leave Moray by 11:00 so you reach the salt pans and the river with daylight to spare.

points.name: Moray terraces
points.note: About 3,385 m. Three round amphitheatres of Inca terraces, thought to be a crop laboratory; walk the rim before you set off east.

points.name: Maras village
points.note: Adobe village with a large white church on the plaza: food and drinks. The path to the salt pans leaves the road past the church.

points.name: Maras salt pans
points.note: Salineras de Maras: thousands of salt pools fed by a salty spring, in a side valley of the Urubamba. Salt for sale; no work in the pools on Sundays.
